checks: Zero weights may be omitted, and positive-radius balls at the retained marks give an interior ball at the combined mark. Every prefix in the projection of int K has an interior lift. A supporting hyperplane at an interior point of its slice would have normal supported on the prefix coordinates and would contradict prefix interiority.

Dominated convergence on one box gives continuous positive marginals at interior prefixes. At j=d the assertion uses the escort density itself. A convex combination with an interior prefix lift brings each projected section endpoint into the open section. The conditional CDF thus goes from zero to one, since Fubini gives the exact prefix mass. Its Borel inverse follows by comparison with CDF values, and its own-coordinate derivative is the reciprocal positive conditional density.

Recursive inversion maps the entire cube onto int K and the diagonal derivative product telescopes to 1/ρ(X). The accepted proof's Borel triangular formula applies to each X_i and S, including when derivatives in other coordinates do not exist. The boundary of K has zero volume, so the escort mass and mean are unchanged by using int K. Substitution on the Borel image U_S, together with U_S⊆M, suffices.

Finite Hölder first gives J_S≥[Σ_i λ_i E_i^(1/d)L_i(X_i)^((d+2)/d)]^d. Jensen uses the weights λ_i E_i^(1/d)/A, giving J_S≥A^d L̄^(d+2). The escort mass identities give mean L̄=1, and its barycenter identities give mean S=y and hence mean B=1. Hölder with d+2 and (d+2)/(d+1) gives ∫L̄^(d+2)B^(−d−1)≥1 for every positive admissible target denominator.

At the attained target denominator, equality of endpoints forces each intervening nonnegative integral gap to vanish. Positivity of B and positive weights give equality almost everywhere in each diagonal AM–GM row and in Jensen. Column normalization makes b_ij/b_1j independent of j. The product identity and equal denominators give the fixed factor c_i=(E_i/E_1)^(1/d), also directly when d=1.

For each chosen direction e the first-coordinate ratio is a function of u_1 alone, so Fubini gives derivative equality almost everywhere in one dimension. Continuity of the derivatives gives the identity everywhere on (0,1), and integrating determines the translation from the escort means. Positive marginal density on the full interior of the projection interval gives its actual support endpoint. The factor c_i is independent of frame, so equality of support functions follows by treating each e separately.

Centered homothety gives M−y=(Σ_i λ_i c_i)(K_1−y_1); covariance makes this sufficient for equality. Distinct marks on a fixed body would force scale one by volume, and a nonzero translation cannot preserve a bounded body. For an actual compact convex fiber at the weighted base, inclusion and the interior ball make the containing-body argument valid. Equality in the actual-fiber bound holds exactly when the actual target equals the Minkowski combination and the positive-weight marked inputs are homothetic.

For two uniform inputs, this fact gives a centroid-mean capped transport and a true-target-covariance bound. Its cap supplies the unmarked volume lower bound, while the reviewed theorem concerns the minimized projective volume at the transported mark and includes noncentroid inputs.

For same-parity endpoint fibers with exact ordinary midpoint Brunn–Minkowski volume, its proof identifies the actual midpoint body and its centroid and gives ordinary homothety. Ordinary exact midpoint volume can recover its fiber rigidity from the reviewed theorem together with E≤volume and equality at the centroid, but the older conclusion does not supply the reviewed energy inequality.
